test.title: login API returns a token
test.error:
Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality
Expected: 200
Received: 423

triage.reason: The API returned HTTP 423 (Locked), which signals the account itself is unusable rather than a wrong response body or a stale test. The test posts valid-looking credentials to the real login endpoint and expecting 200 is reasonable, so the test code is not at fault. The credential is a shared public-sandbox demo account (customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com), and such accounts commonly get locked by other users' failed login attempts — a shared account that is locked, which is an environment cause. Consistent failure across all 3 attempts matches a persistent lockout rather than flakiness. A real app bug is the alternative if the service wrongly locks valid accounts, which is why confidence is not high.
triage.evidence: "Expected: 200 / Received: 423" at `expect(response.status()).toBe(200);` for POST https://api.practicesoftwaretesting.com/users/login with data { email: 'customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com', password: 'pass123' }
triage.next_step: Reproduce the login outside Playwright (curl -X POST https://api.practicesoftwaretesting.com/users/login -d '{"email":"customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com","password":"pass123"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json"); if it still returns 423, wait out the lockout or switch the test to a freshly registered, test-owned account instead of the shared demo login.

test.error:
Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.

Call log:
test.pageSnapshot:
- generic [active] [ref=e1]:
  - heading "Not Found" [level=1] [ref=e2]
  - paragraph [ref=e3]: The requested URL was not found on this server.
  - separator [ref=e4]
  - generic [ref=e5]: Apache/2.4.52 (Ubuntu) Server at with-bugs.practicesoftwaretesting.com Port 443

triage.reason: The locator timeout is a symptom, not the cause: the page the test navigated to never rendered. The accessibility tree shows Apache's own default 404 page for /auth/login, so the login page the test needs is not being served. The connection, DNS and TLS all succeeded, which rules out an environment failure, and the identical failure on all 3 attempts rules out flakiness. Because this is a client-routed SPA, a merely wrong path would normally still return index.html and render the app's own not-found view; Apache's stock 404 instead indicates the app is not served at that route (broken deploy or missing rewrite/fallback). The alternative that the login route was renamed and goto('/auth/login') is stale (broken script) is possible but less consistent with a server-level 404, hence medium confidence.
triage.evidence: Page at failure: 'heading "Not Found" [level=1]' / 'The requested URL was not found on this server.' / 'Apache/2.4.52 (Ubuntu) Server at with-bugs.practicesoftwaretesting.com Port 443', against the navigation at login-page.ts:17 'await this.page.goto('/auth/login');' — error line: 'Error: locator.fill: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email address' })'.
triage.next_step: Open https://with-bugs.practicesoftwaretesting.com/auth/login directly in a browser (and curl -I the same URL) to confirm the server returns 404 for the login route; if it does, report the broken deploy/missing SPA rewrite rule to the dev team, and at the same time verify the configured baseURL and the app's current login path to rule out a stale route in login-page.ts.

triage.reason: The mock never intercepted the products request, so the app legitimately had products to show and the empty-state text was correctly absent. The accessibility tree shows nine real products and 3 pages of pagination, which is impossible if `route.fulfill({ json: { data: [] } })` had been applied. The route glob `'**/products'` does not match the real request URL, which carries a query string (page/sort/filter params); Playwright matches the glob against the full URL including the query. Fixing the pattern (e.g. `'**/products?*'`, `'**/products*'` or a regex) is a test change, not an app change — there is no evidence the app mishandles an empty list, because it never received one.
triage.evidence: Test code: `await page.route('**/products', (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { data: [] } }));` — yet the failing page shows `link "ECO Combination Pliers CO₂: A B C D E $14.15"` ... `navigation "Pagination": - listitem: You're on page 1`, i.e. real server data, while the assertion `getByText('There are no products found.')` reports "element(s) not found".
triage.next_step: Add `page.on('request', r => console.log(r.url()))` (or open the trace's Network tab) to capture the actual products request URL, then widen the route pattern to match it — e.g. `page.route(/\/products(\?|$)/, ...)` — and re-run to confirm the empty-state message appears.

That is why getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Search' }) never resolves and fill() times out. Neighbouring labels are mangled the same way ("Contakt", " Sorth") and the page banner says "Bug Hunting Mode - Find & Report Bugs!", so the mislabelled/unlabelled search controls look like injected app defects rather than an outdated locator.
